Question B-003-019-009.

Why the correct answer is right: An insulated shorting stick with an inline resistor keeps the operator away from the charge and limits discharge current to reduce arcs and damage.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Use a long screwdriver with an insulated handle": A screwdriver provides essentially no current limiting, so a charged capacitor can arc violently and damage parts or burn the worker.
- sourceIndex 2: "Use an insulated wire with alligator clips on each end": A plain clip lead also lacks a series resistor, causing an uncontrolled surge current and possible arc when it touches the capacitor.
- sourceIndex 3: "Allow time for bleeder resistors to discharge the capacitors": Bleeders can fail or take longer than expected. Waiting alone is not a verified safe discharge method before work.
